signal: The AI stack is converging on agentic coding at lower cost, while the hard engineering shifts toward inference efficiency, hardware co-design, and stronger isolation around increasingly capable autonomous systems.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 3.7 Flash for coding and agent workflows
stories.summary: Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash on August 13, positioning it as a lower-cost model for software coding and autonomous multi-step business workflows, with an introductory API price of $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens.
stories.whyItMatters: The frontier is moving toward cheaper models that can stay inside long-running tool loops. For production agents, completed-task reliability and total workflow cost are becoming more useful metrics than raw benchmark quality.
stories.attention: Very high — lower-cost frontier agent model

stories.title: DeepSeek formally releases V4 Pro with stronger agent capabilities
stories.summary: DeepSeek released V4-Pro-0813 across API, app and web, saying the update substantially improves agent capabilities while introducing tiered peak and off-peak API pricing.
stories.whyItMatters: DeepSeek is competing on both capability and serving economics. Its support for agent-oriented workloads reinforces the case for keeping model providers replaceable and benchmarking real tool-use trajectories rather than assuming the most expensive model should own every stage.

stories.title: Taiwan reports an AI-assisted cyberattack on government systems
stories.summary: Taiwan said attackers used a hybrid of manual operations and AI-agent assistance in a July campaign against government agencies; investigators said the incident came from overseas and affected units successfully contained it.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the shift security teams have been preparing for: AI agents can compress reconnaissance, credential discovery and exploitation into faster operational loops. Defensive systems need machine-speed detection, strong identity boundaries, detailed tool telemetry and rapid containment.
stories.attention: Very high — AI-assisted attacks move into real operations

stories.title: Anthropic explores buying Decart to deepen inference and performance engineering
stories.summary: Anthropic is in early talks to acquire Nvidia-backed Decart AI, whose work spans AI infrastructure, optimization and world models; Reuters reports Decart's team would join Anthropic's inference and performance organization if a deal closes.
stories.whyItMatters: Frontier labs are increasingly pulling optimization, hardware-software co-design and model serving closer to the core model team. At scale, inference performance is becoming a strategic product capability rather than an interchangeable infrastructure layer.

stories.title: KVGov isolates tenants without giving up most prefix-cache efficiency
stories.summary: A new arXiv paper demonstrates production-scale timing leakage from shared KV-prefix caches and proposes per-principal salted cache keys; the authors estimate a boundary-salting design can retain about 93% of prefix-cache benefit while removing cross-principal signals.
stories.whyItMatters: Prefix caching is an optimization with a tenant-isolation boundary hidden inside it. Multi-tenant inference platforms should treat cache identity and reuse policy as security architecture, not only performance tuning.

takeaway: Design AI platforms for rapid model substitution and increasingly autonomous execution. Put routing and cost telemetry above the model layer, and put isolation, cache governance, observability and containment below it.
